one_line: The Travancore ruler who crushed the Ettuveetil Pillamar and centralised royal power in early 18th‑century southern Kerala.

appearance.age_look: Looks around 30, lean yet well-muscled, medium height with a poised, athletic build.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp jawline, warm medium‑brown complexion, straight nose, expressive dark eyes with slightly thick brows; a small sandalwood tilak on the forehead; default expression calm but steely, with a faint determined smirk.
appearance.hair: Long black hair oiled and smoothed back into a low knot at the nape, partly hidden under a deep red silk headcloth (mundu-style turban) folded flat around the crown with one neat tail hanging behind the right ear.
appearance.costume: Wears an off‑white handwoven cotton double mundu wrapped tightly around the waist and falling to the ankles with a thin gold border, paired with a long‑sleeved light cream angarkha-style upper cloth tied diagonally and kept modestly closed, over which a rich deep red silk kasavu shawl with broad gold border is draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the waist; around his waist a dark green cloth belt binds the scabbard, while his feet wear simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is restrained yet royal—thin gold chain at the neck, a pair of small round gold earrings, a single broad gold bangle on the right wrist and a simple signet ring on the left hand.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved Malabar-style sword with a simple steel blade, a plain but polished iron hilt and a dark brown wooden scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn at his left hip and often held resting across his forearms.

ref_desc: Marthanda Varma is a lean, medium‑brown man of about 30 with long black hair in a low knot under a deep red headcloth, wearing an off‑white double mundu, cream angarkha, red‑and‑gold shawl, minimal gold jewellery and a Malabar‑style sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet of Marthanda Varma from early 18th‑century Travancore: a lean, athletic man around 30 with an oval face, medium‑brown skin, sharp jawline, straight nose and expressive dark eyes, bearing a small sandalwood tilak and a calm but steely expression with a faint smirk. His long black hair is oiled and drawn into a low knot at the nape, partly covered by a deep red silk headcloth folded flat around the crown, with one neat tail hanging behind his right ear. He wears an off‑white handwoven cotton double mundu with a thin gold border wrapped securely around his waist and reaching his ankles, and a long‑sleeved light cream angarkha‑style upper cloth tied diagonally and fully closed for modesty. Over this, drape a rich deep red silk kasavu shawl with a broad gold border from his left shoulder across the chest and around the waist, hinting at royal authority without being overly ornate. Cinch his waist with a dark green cloth belt that supports a dark brown wooden scabbard with simple brass fittings. Put simple brown leather sandals on his feet. Add restrained jewellery: a thin gold neck chain, small round gold earrings, one broad gold bangle on his right wrist and a plain signet ring on his left hand. His signature weapon is a slightly curved Malabar‑style sword with a plain polished iron hilt and steel blade, worn at his left hip and shown also in his hand resting lightly across his forearms. Use a palette dominated by off‑white, deep red, gold, dark green and brown, and show him from multiple angles to clearly present face, hair, costume and sword in a consistent design.
